tasks.title: Settings reports meet the heartbeat deadline through one cancellable polling lane
tasks.spec: ## Repository: status, Behavior (D1-D4), Checks (harness and tests 1-9), and all Completion evidence (Base, Red, Green, Scope checker, Fixture proof, docs, delayed-answer runs and test_cpu_s); Required behavior R1-R8; Counterexamples C1-C11; Scope/Non-goals; Risks; Performance impact; Security impact; Rollout order; Acceptance evidence (feature).

acceptance.expected: Before any implementation edit, record this full SHA as immutable BASE and save it with file tools outside the checkout, for example /tmp/status-844-base.sha; reuse the saved value in later sessions and include it in the PR. The expected starting main is bcd83dad0975954b687ce89fc8ad369ba3a94e8a or a later main commit. Never move BASE after an edit or commit. Scope acceptance below requires it to be an ancestor of HEAD and origin/main. All temporary scripts, logs, fixtures and the red worktree stay outside the checkout; only the four task files may change.

acceptance.command: git worktree add /tmp/status-base "$BASE" && cp src/settings-poll.heartbeat.test.ts /tmp/status-base/src/ && (cd /tmp/status-base && bun install --frozen-lockfile && bun test src/settings-poll.heartbeat.test.ts)
acceptance.expected: Red evidence, before relying on the fix: copy only the new suite into the base worktree; it imports only names available on BASE, never REPORT_LEAD_MS or another new export. Frozen install succeeds and the real base poller fails behavioral assertions: test 1's 60000/1000 and 60000/4000 cases report gaps 62000 and 68000; tests 2, 3, 4, 5 and shutdown 7b-7e fail; all six test 9 cases fail with old read gaps 60000, 61000, 64000, 65000, 64000 and 59000. The other four test 1 cases, test 6, shutdown 7a and both test 8 cases pass as controls. An install, compile or import error is not red evidence. Save command, failing test names and assertion texts for the PR. A focused suite may fail the global coverage gate independently of these assertions. Keep /tmp/status-base until the delayed-answer and test CPU comparisons are complete.

All tests pass, 0 fail; the full-suite coverage gate is checked by bun run check, not this focused command. Test-only harness uses an injected clock starting at 0, chronological timer advancement with promise draining, cancellable fake fetch (including preconnect), valid contract responses, held requests, counting readLocal/apply and the real startSettingsPoll/resolveSettings. No real network or waits and no clock advance inside fetch. Measure every adjacent PUT fetch-start gap, not completion/body timestamps or averages, and assert nonempty samples. Test 1 covers pollMs 60000 and DEFAULT_SETTINGS_POLL_MS (asserted equal to 15000), each with equal read/report latency 0, 1000 and 4000; at least 4 report starts per case, maximum gap <= 60000, maximum in-flight requests <= 1, minimum read gap >= 54000 or >= 15000 respectively. Test 2 alternates instant and 4000 ms reads, then instant and reads held to the 5000 ms timeout, at pollMs 60000 with instant reports; each case has at least 4 reports, gaps <= 60000 and no overlap. Test 3 uses instant reads and reports delayed 4000 or held to timeout 5000 at pollMs 60000; gaps <= 60000, no overlap and later reads prove recovery. Test 4 uses pollMs 120000 with a token and latency 1000; at least 4 reports and gaps <= 60000 (heartbeat only; the cap is tested without a token). Test 5 holds the second read at pollMs 1000, calls pollNow three times, observes no overlapping GET, releases it and observes exactly one extra poll shared by all callers; their promises resolve only after that report completes and a further background GET occurs after advancing 1000. Test 6 throws from resolve after its first two calls; at pollMs 60000 over 120000 fake ms there are at most 4 GETs, preventing a stale-anchor spin. Test 7 covers (a) idle stop: zero later fetches and empty timer queue after 300000; (b) stop during read: aborted signal, no report, unchanged local-read/apply counts and empty timer queue after 300000; (c) stop during report: aborted signal, no later fetch, empty timer queue after 300000 and no 'status settings report failed' log; (d) queued pollNow at stop resolves without a request; (e) pollNow after stop resolves with zero fetches and repeated stop does not throw. Test 8 has no token at pollMs 60000 and 120000; zero fetches, isReady true and readLocal times exactly [0, 60000, 120000, 180000, 240000, 300000] in both cases. Test 9 uses a token, instant reports and at least 5 GET starts: at pollMs 60000 with reads 0, 1000, 4000 and timeout 5000, all read gaps equal 54000, 55000, 58000 and 59000 respectively and each next GET minus previous PUT equals 54000; at pollMs 120000/read 4000 these literals are 58000/54000; at pollMs 55000/read 4000 they are 55000/51000. All expectations are test literals independent of the implementation's scheduling formula.

exit 0 on the branch using pinned Bun 1.4.0: frozen install, Biome/ESLint/workflow lint, strict root/e2e typechecks and full tests pass with the existing 0.8 line coverage threshold and cognitive complexity limit 15. Existing test files, dependencies, lockfile and tooling remain unchanged; no gate is weakened.

All tests in the three unchanged suites pass, 0 fail; any global coverage shortfall from this focused invocation is not a test failure (the full suite must pass its gate). Existing settings, readiness, ETag, 304/404, last-good, local-file and report behavior remains compatible, including timers.includes(15000) with the existing fixed clock.

acceptance.command: git diff "$BASE" HEAD -- src/settings-poll.ts README.md docs/configuration.md
acceptance.expected: Review committed implementation against D1-D4/R1-R8: next idle-lane timer uses max(0, due-now); without token due=pollStart+min(pollMs,60000); with token due=min(pollStart+min(pollMs,60000),anchor+54000). Record pollStart per poll and anchor just before report fetch; a poll that sends no report uses its own start as anchor. REPORT_LEAD_MS=SETTINGS_TIMEOUT_MS+1000=6000 is internal, with its reserve comment; existing SETTINGS_TIMEOUT_MS=5000, REPORT_HEARTBEAT_MS=60000 and exports remain, with corrected heartbeat comment. One lane handles initial/timer/manual polls, clears an old timer on poll start, coalesces at most one waiting manual poll, ignores a timer firing during a poll, catches/logs poll failures as today and re-arms from the just-finished poll. Each poll shares one AbortController between read/report. Synchronous idempotent stop clears timer and aborts that controller; guards prevent local reread/apply/report/re-arm after stop, queued/later pollNow resolves without work and aborted report logs no failure. No changes to SettingsPollDeps/SettingsPoll signatures, report body/buildReport arguments, endpoints/methods/headers, redirect manual, timeout/schedule/maxBytes/validation, ETag, readiness, precedence, rejection/404 handling, public responses, polling settings range/default or browser/API polling. Security impact remains no; no new route, auth, parser, dependency, log text, Docker or CI change. Docs update only the specified settings paragraph and README Live page settings timing clauses, preserving the rest. They promise report starts at most 60 s apart whatever HTTP time is within the 5000 ms request timeout, configured start-to-start cadence up to 54000, report-to-next-read <=54 s, and 54 to 59 s read spacing above 54000, never above the configured interval and potentially faster, not always faster. pollMs 55000 with 4000 ms reads keeps 55000. Only status changes; notify #824 and all other repositories stay independent.

acceptance.command: grep -nE 'every 54 s|about 54 s|at most (about )?54 s apart' README.md docs/configuration.md
acceptance.expected: No output, exit 1: neither document promises a fixed/about/at-most 54 s read-to-read interval. Reviewer also reads both changed sentences against D1 Two bounds/R8: 54 s as an upper bound refers only to previous report start to next read start; no sentence claims reads above 54000 are always faster than configured.

acceptance.command: grep -c '54 to 59 s' README.md docs/configuration.md && grep -c 'can be faster' docs/configuration.md && grep -c '60 s' README.md
acceptance.expected: exit 0; first grep prints a count >=1 for each document; second and third counts are each >=1. Both docs explain read spacing depends on the previous read time; configuration states it can be faster when 54 s plus previous read time is less than the configured interval, otherwise it keeps that interval; values from 60000 up behave the same. README explicitly states the 60 s report-start guarantee within the existing timeout.

Create this temporary orchestration/measurement script with file tools outside the checkout to implement Completion evidence's Delayed-answer run, then run it against BASE in /tmp/status-base and the branch. Fake api listens on 127.0.0.1 and delays each settings/report answer 4000 ms; settings replies are valid 200 with wire header and etag e1, then 304 for matching If-None-Match; reports reply 204 with wire header. Launch each service with bun start, PULSE_API_URL pointing at the fake api, dummy PULSE_STATUS_API_TOKEN and a free PORT. Log every request arrival time. Run A: PULSE_STATUS_SETTINGS_POLL_MS=15000, three 300000 ms windows per side from the first GET; base GET count 14 +/-1, branch 20 +/-1, PUT count equals GET count +/-1; base gaps 23000, branch 15000. Measure status-process CPU as utime+stime from /proc/<pid>/stat fields 14/15 (10 ms ticks) at first GET and 300000 ms later, report side medians and CPU ms/poll; branch median exceeds base median by at most 300 ms (expected well under 100). Run B: PULSE_STATUS_SETTINGS_POLL_MS=60000 until >=4 report starts per side; first PUT around 4000; all report and read arrival gaps 68000 +/-50 on base and 58000 +/-50 on branch; each GET minus previous PUT 64000 +/-50 on base and 54000 +/-50 on branch. Every branch report gap <60000. Ctrl-C gives clean exit. Record commands, request-time logs, counts, CPU and exit results in the PR; investigate failures/noise rather than dropping gates. This measures the slow-api request-rate/CPU risk, which the fast local benchmark and test CPU cannot establish.

acceptance.command: for run in 1 2 3; do (cd /tmp/status-base && /usr/bin/time -f '%U %S' bun test); done; for run in 1 2 3; do /usr/bin/time -f '%U %S' bun test; done
acceptance.expected: Record all three user+system CPU measurements per side and their medians in the PR; branch-minus-base median is under 0.2 s (test_cpu_s, expected increase under 0.1 s). For the BASE measurements remove the copied, untracked heartbeat suite from /tmp/status-base after red evidence, so BASE measures its unchanged suite; the branch includes the new suite. Production base code stays unchanged. No startup, RSS, image or fast-local load benchmark metric is expected to move; the optional full api bench A/B is not a required gate.
